clue.text: Forcibly restrain two thousand disrupting traffic

indicators.note: disrupting means breaking into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to coerce is to restrain or compel by force
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two thousand is MM

explanation.surface: Police forcibly hold back two thousand protesters who are blocking the traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as a noun means trade or dealing in goods, which is what business between buyers and sellers is.

clue.text: Star seen in beaver fur

definitions.meaning: a bright star in the constellation Gemini, named after one of the heavenly twins
an old name for beaver pelt, or for a hat made from it

explanation.surface: A celebrity is spotted wearing a beaver-fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: One twin of Gemini names a bright star in that constellation, and the same word was used for beaver pelt and hats made of it.

clue.text: Mule is chomping our dish

indicators.note: chomping means chewing noisily, so the letters of these words are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A mule munches its way through the family's breakfast bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit, Swiss in origin.

clue.text: One lifting the lid will have a big surprise!

definitions.text: One lifting the lid will have a big surprise!

parts.words: One lifting the lid will have a big surprise!
parts.note: the lid is an eyelid rather than the cover of a box; the thing that makes someone raise their eyelids wide is a startling revelation

explanation.surface: Whoever opens the box is in for a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation that startles someone into seeing the truth, literally making the eyelids part.

clue.text: Stubborn' but has to get over reading difficulty

annotationWithheld.why: 'Stubborn, but has to get over reading difficulty (5,7)': 'Stubborn' defines and 'get over' gives CROSS, but nothing in 'reading difficulty' gives GRAINED, and the rest is no clear second definition
annotationWithheld.clue: Stubborn' but has to get over reading difficulty

clue.text: Out at elbow

parts.note: the phrase usually means shabby, with sleeves worn through; here it describes arms bent with the elbows pointing outwards, hands on hips

explanation.definitionFit: With hands on hips the elbows jut outwards, the posture this word describes.

clue.text: Knife skill demonstrated by the chef' say?

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase before it is to be heard rather than read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: cookery is the skill a chef shows

explanation.surface: A chef shows off clever knife work.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved Nepalese blade, famously carried by Gurkha soldiers.

clue.text: Many too wary to travel by fast route

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, can stand for a large number

indicators.note: to travel signals that the letters of the following words move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Lots of drivers are too nervous to use the fast road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a motorway is a high-speed multi-lane road, like a US freeway.
explanation.definitionFit: A British multi-lane highway built for fast long-distance driving.

clue.text: Does Bess panic' with bee in her bonnet?

indicators.note: a panic throws everything into disorder, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Bess flies into a panic when a bee gets into her hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a bee in one's bonnet is an idiom for being fixated on a single idea.

clue.text: Kind of key that might be hidden in the cupboard

definitions.meaning: a master key filed down so it opens many locks

definitions.text: that might be hidden in the cupboard
definitions.meaning: from the idiom for a shameful family secret kept hidden in a closet

explanation.surface: A special key might be kept out of sight in the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A master key that opens many locks has this name, and so does the bony frame in the idiom for a hidden guilty secret.

clue.text: Put on by one in a bustle?

definitions.text: Put on by one in a bustle?

parts.words: Put on by one in a bustle?
parts.note: a bustle suggests a Victorian dress pad, but here it is a hurry; the British saying for hurrying up is to put a certain kind of bladed footwear on

explanation.surface: Something worn by a lady in a Victorian bustle dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bustle' looks like the padded Victorian skirt; it means a rush. The British idiom 'get your skates on' means hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladed or wheeled boots for gliding, which a British saying tells someone in a rush to put on.

clue.text: I can collapse after first payment — a levy reportedly prompting these reactions

indicators.note: after places the scrambled letters behind the opening letter of payment
first picks out the opening letter of the word payment
collapse means fall into a heap, so the letters of these words fall into a new order
reportedly means as heard, so the phrase before it is spelt by its sound

parts.note: a levy is a tax, so these words give 'a tax'

explanation.surface: Someone collapses after paying a new tax demand, which brings on fits of terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse' turns I CAN into ANIC; 'reportedly' says 'a tax' is heard as the word for assaults.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden bouts of overwhelming fear, with racing heart and breathlessness, are the reactions meant.

clue.text: Flowery name for beef sauce?

parts.note: an ox is the animal that gives beef
sauce in British usage means cheek or impudence, as does lip

explanation.surface: A fancy menu title for a beef dish served with gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' and 'lip' are both British words for cheeky backchat.
explanation.definitionFit: A primula, a spring wildflower related to the cowslip and primrose.

clue.text: Europeans filter back into health resorts

indicators.note: into puts the turned word inside the word for resorts

parts.note: spas are health resorts

indicators.note: back means the word for filter is read from right to left

parts.note: to drain is to filter liquid off

explanation.surface: Tourists from the continent trickle back to the spa towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Europeans' is the definition, not the filter; 'back' turns the word for filter round (NIARD) before 'into' places it within the resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Spain, a country of Europe.

clue.text: Irate lunatic oddly incoherent

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, so the letters of these words are set in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An angry madman babbles nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to express oneself clearly in speech, which is what incoherent means.

clue.text: In this lake' bobbing around' the French trawl with us

indicators.note: bobbing around, like a boat on choppy water, signals the letters are jumbled

parts.note: le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: French fishermen trawl alongside us on a lake, bobbing about in the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of LE, TRAWL and US gives a lake in the English Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: The second-largest body of water in Cumbria's Lake District, in north-west England.

clue.text: Hide from girl — having put letters in wrong order

definitions.text: having put letters in wrong order

indicators.note: from means the hide comes on from the girl, following it

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
a pelt is an animal's hide

explanation.surface: A girl hides a note in which she has jumbled the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Written with letters wrong or out of place, a spelling error.

clue.text: With this' sexton smashed oriental object buried inside?

annotationWithheld.why: 'With this, sexton smashed oriental object buried inside? (5,3)': the anagram of SEXTON plus E (oriental) gives seven letters; no clue word supplies the A the answer needs
annotationWithheld.clue: With this' sexton smashed oriental object buried inside?

clue.text: No end to it — blame inner turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil is confusion, so the letters of these words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Guilt and inner turmoil seem to go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end to' stands for the adjective meaning endless; 'it' joins BLAME INNER as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless or seemingly everlasting, with no finish in sight.

clue.text: Clay duck turned up on tree' up north

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the turned duck follows the turned tree
up north in a down answer means read from bottom to top, so this word is backwards too

parts.note: an oak is a tree

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means read upwards, so the word is backwards

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so nil

explanation.surface: A duck is spotted perched in a tree somewhere in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up north' turns OAK into KAO and 'turned up' turns NIL into LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine white china clay used for porcelain and in medicine.

clue.text: Hits out at live character thought dead by Pyramus

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A blow lands on the woman Pyramus believed had been killed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Ovid's story, staged in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, Pyramus kills himself believing a lion has killed his beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyramus's lover in the Ovid legend, whom he wrongly believed slain by a lion.

clue.text: Seen to crumple and smell' when growing old

indicators.note: to crumple means to fall into a heap, so the letters of the word fall into a new order

parts.note: a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Things start to crumple and smell musty as they age.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageing and deteriorating, a term from biology for the decline of cells and organisms.

clue.text: The going rate for an amphetamine

definitions.meaning: the rate at which something goes, its velocity
street slang for amphetamine, the stimulant drug

explanation.surface: The price paid on the street for a stimulant drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Velocity is the rate of going, and the same short word is slang for the stimulant drug.

clue.text: Fury coming to a head in Scotland

definitions.meaning: a headland: the cape at the far north-western tip of mainland Scotland

explanation.surface: Anger comes to a head north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Great anger, and the name of the cape at the north-western corner of the Scottish mainland.

clue.text: Hedges woman's planted around a dam

indicators.note: planted around means set on either side, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, with the possessive gives Eve's
d. is the pedigree abbreviation for dam, the mother of an animal, as s. is for sire

explanation.surface: A woman has hedges planted around a reservoir dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hedges' looks like a garden noun; it is the verb meaning dodges. In horse pedigrees d. stands for dam.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to avoid committing oneself, dodging a straight answer.

clue.text: Sinks full of coal?

definitions.meaning: deliberately sends a ship to the bottom by holing it
describes the buckets kept by a hearth, filled with fuel

explanation.surface: Kitchen basins loaded up with coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Holing one's own ship to send it to the bottom has this name, as do the hearthside buckets for carrying fuel.

clue.text: Use curtains in attempt to be fashionable

indicators.note: use instructs the solver to employ the next word as a piece placed somewhere
in puts the word for the finish inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
curtains is slang for the end, as in 'it's curtains for him'

explanation.surface: Hanging new curtains in an effort to look stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to date and in style, following the latest vogue.

clue.text: Set off' have a row — then separate

indicators.note: off means out of true, so the letters of the word are disturbed

parts.note: a range is a row or line, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Friends set off together, quarrel, then part company.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate, driving apart people who were once close.
